title: Mahi-Mahi with Mango-Lime Sauce and Coconut Rice
description: Mango puree makes a mellow golden poaching sauce for mahi-mahi over rice softened with light coconut milk.
equipment: Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: skinless mahi-mahi fillet
ingredients.note: Weight after skin and pin bones are removed. Divide into two even portions about 3/4 to 1 inch thick. Fully thaw before cooking.

ingredients.name: peeled ripe mango flesh
ingredients.note: Weight after peeling and pitting. Choose a low-fiber ripe mango.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Choose unsalted plain meat-and-water broth without a vegetable blend.

steps.title: Soften the coconut rice
steps.text: Warm {rice} and {coconut} in the covered saucepan over low heat for 4–7 minutes until creamy and at least 165°F throughout. Stir once and keep covered.

steps.title: Make the mango base
steps.text: Blend {mango} and {broth} smooth in a deep jug. Pour into the HexClad and bring to a gentle simmer. Set aside a spoonful in a clean covered cup for resting the fish.

steps.title: Poach the mahi-mahi
steps.text: Nestle {fish} into the mango base, spoon the liquid over the top and cover. Poach at a bare simmer for about 7–13 minutes, checking after 6 minutes. Pull each portion at 135°F.

steps.title: Rest the fish
steps.text: Place the portions on a warm plate and moisten with the reserved mango base and cover. Rest for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Boil the poaching liquid
steps.text: Bring the mango base in the HexClad to a full boil for 1 minute, stirring along the bottom.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} until completely smooth.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish with basil and lime
steps.text: Stir {lime} and {basil} into the warm mango sauce off heat.

steps.title: Check carryover and doneness
steps.text: After resting, check each thickest center for about 140°F. Open a natural seam with a fork. The center should be opaque and separate easily into flakes. If either cue is unclear or the center is below 140°F, finish covered in hot sauce in the HexClad over low heat to a measured 145°F, checking every minute.

steps.title: Spoon into bowls
steps.text: Spoon the coconut rice into shallow bowls and top with the mahi-mahi. Ladle mango sauce over the fish and rice.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/2 cups of sauce for two in addition to the coconut rice. Make ahead: Puree mango and broth up to a day ahead. Refrigerate separately from the fish. Refrigerate in shallow portions within 2 hours. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze up to 1 month with the rice underneath and the fish covered in mango sauce. A splash of water loosens the rice as it reheats. Fridge reheat: Warm a portion covered in its sauce over medium-low heat in the HexClad. Add a little water if it has thickened in storage. Check from 5 minutes and heat to 165°F at the coldest center. Freezer reheat: If frozen, thaw the covered portion in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge method. Option A uses a little lime. For gentler Option B, omit it and finish with extra minced basil. The dish is dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 269 kcal, 29.3 g protein, 29.1 g total carbohydrate, 3.3 g fat, 1.2 g fiber, 152 mg sodium. Includes both the fish and its full share of sauce and any rice or potatoes listed. Sodium varies with the broth.
